problem: The text says every input can be treated as a 'sum of shifted impulses' in continuous time. In continuous time the representation is an integral of shifted impulses, not a sum.
fix: Say 'an integral of shifted impulses' and write x(t)=∫x(τ)δ(t−τ)dτ.

problem: The convolution integral y(t)=∫x(τ)h(t−τ)dτ has no limits, and τ is reused without saying it is now a dummy integration variable; Section 1 defined τ as the delay.
fix: Write y(t)=∫_{−∞}^{∞} x(τ)h(t−τ)dτ and state that τ here is a dummy integration variable, separate from the delay τ used in the time-invariance test.

problem: The phrase 'y(t)=x(2t) has no t in the multiplier' is misleading: the argument 2t does contain t. The intended point is that there is no standalone t term outside the input.
fix: Say 'y(t)=x(2t) has no standalone t term added outside the input, but it is time-varying.'

problem: The name 'zero-input test' can be confused with the zero-input response, which is the response due to initial conditions and is a different idea.
fix: Call it the 'zero-input zero-output check' or simply say 'if the input is zero, the output must be zero'.
